# [reference] Leaf spring and shackle repair

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Jack up the vehicle and replace the leaf spring by removing shackle bolts and U-bolts. [t1048]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Jack up the vehicle and place rear ends on jack stands.
2. Position a jack under the axle to find a height where the leaf spring has no force in either direction.
3. [Partial] Remove the shackle bolts connecting the spring to the frame or crossmember.
4. [Partial] Unbolt the U-bolts securing the lower control arm (or front of leaf pack) to the axle.
5. [Partial] Install the new leaf spring and secure it with fresh U-bolts.
6. [Partial] Tighten the nuts on the U-bolt ends first, then tighten the shackle bolts last.
7. Use a jack under the axle or body to adjust ride height as needed before final tightening.

_Procedure reported by [t1048]._

## Tools

- Jack [t1048]
- Jack stands [t1048]

## Parts

- [Partial] Leaf spring, new [t1048]
- U-bolts, new, one-time use: Cut off excess and mangle threads to prevent backing down [t1048]

## Tips & gotchas

- Work on one side at a time. [t1048]
- Remove the wheel if easier access is needed. [t1048]
- Spray parts with PB Blaster a week before starting, twice daily for best results. [t1048]
